key_insight: Adaptive hyperreduction accelerates finite element identification of neural constitutive laws while preserving accuracy as network weights evolve.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can identify material behavior from structural force data while accommodating arbitrary geometries, boundary conditions, and sparse or noisy measurements.
method: Combine proper orthogonal decomposition with energy-conserving sampling and weighting.
Adapt reduced trial spaces and sampled elements during optimization, using reduced-model adjoint sensitivities.
Use a neural energy architecture that guarantees polyconvexity, coercivity, and non-negativity by construction.
evidence_signal: Across two experimental datasets and one synthetic 3D example, the method reproduced reaction forces and predicted displacements; two-phase training fell from 9 hours to 41 minutes without loss of accuracy.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on updating the reduced basis and sampled elements as the constitutive network changes during training.
paper_title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials
